display.title: Asarah B'Teves: A Time to Be Sad and a Time to Hope
display.summary_short: Why we remember the sad days of Jewish history: the siege of Yerushalayim that began on the tenth of Teves, and Hashem's promise to turn these fasts into Yomim Tovim.
display.summary_long: A calendar talk from the Tzivos Hashem radio show. Uncle Yossi walks through the months to Teves and quotes Shlomo HaMelech: there is a time for everything, a time to be happy and also a time to be sad. We remember the hard times of our ancestors not to stay sad but to learn from the past and serve Hashem with a purer heart. On the tenth of Teves the army of Nevuchadnetzar, king of Bavel, surrounded Yerushalayim and sealed its gates, and the people grew weak from hunger. After two and a half years the walls were breached on the seventeenth of Tammuz, and three weeks later, on Tisha B'Av, the Beis HaMikdash was destroyed. As long as we learn Torah and keep mitzvos, Hashem, the Guardian of Israel who never sleeps, protects us. Hashem has promised to turn these fasts into days of joy when Moshiach comes. The fast is this coming Sunday, and everyone calls out 'Ad mosai', 'Until when?', praying to be in Yerushalayim next year.
display.lesson: We remember sad days in order to learn from them and improve, and we pray that Moshiach will turn them into Yomim Tovim.
